cim_eredeti: AI-Integrated Competency Teaching Improves Short-Term Ophthalmology Scores in Randomized Trial
szoveg_eredeti:
AI-Integrated Competency Teaching Improves Short-Term Ophthalmology Scores in Randomized Trial

An educational evaluation conducted in ophthalmology clinical teaching found that an artificial intelligence-supported instruction model organized around job competency cultivation yielded higher short-term scores across theoretical knowledge, practical execution, and clinical performance compared with traditional instruction. The randomized study evaluated an integrated curriculum that combined problem-based learning and case-based learning with artificial intelligence tools. Grounded in job competency development for medical trainees, the curriculum was designed to test whether restructuring clinical ophthalmology education through this combined framework produced measurable gains over standard instructional formats.

The investigation took place at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, focusing on clinical practice within the institution’s Department of Ophthalmology. Over a two-year evaluation period spanning from June 2023 to June 2025, a total of 106 trainees engaged in clinical practice were enrolled in the study. To ensure an unbiased comparative trial, the researchers allocated all 106 participating trainees using a random number table. This procedure divided the cohort into two evenly balanced arms of equal size, creating an observation group containing 53 trainees and a control group containing 53 trainees.

Educational methods differed systematically between the two study arms throughout their clinical practice placements. Participants assigned to the control group received traditional lecture-based teaching paired with conventional problem-based learning and case-based learning techniques. Conversely, trainees assigned to the observation group participated in an educational model that integrated artificial intelligence directly into problem-based and case-based learning formats. Furthermore, the instructional framework in the observation arm was explicitly structured around job competency development, establishing a distinct pedagogical contrast with the lecture-based and conventional methods administered to the control cohort.

To capture the impact of the respective teaching strategies, investigators conducted formal assessments before and after the educational intervention across five core domains. Job competency was measured using the Chinese Clinical Physician Post Competency Questionnaire, tracking overall competency alongside individual dimensional scores. Academic mastery and clinical execution were evaluated through dedicated theoretical knowledge examinations and practical skills assessments. Trainee critical thinking disposition was examined using the Critical Thinking Disposition Inventory-Chinese Version, known as the CTDI-CV. Finally, clinical practice ability was appraised using the Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise, or Mini-CEX, while overall trainee satisfaction with the teaching experience was recorded as an independent outcome.

Following the completion of the educational programs, comparative analyses between the two cohorts demonstrated significant improvements in the observation group across all evaluated parameters. On the Chinese Clinical Physician Post Competency Questionnaire, trainees in the observation group achieved significantly higher total scores and dimensional scores than their peers in the control group, with statistical significance established at P < 0.05. The observation group also attained significantly higher scores on both the theoretical examination and the practical skills performance assessment compared with the control cohort (P < 0.05). These positive differences extended to critical thinking and direct clinical execution, where total scores and subscale scores on the CTDI-CV and the Mini-CEX were significantly improved relative to the control group (P < 0.05). In addition, overall teaching satisfaction was significantly greater among trainees receiving the AI-integrated curriculum (P < 0.05).

In summarizing their findings, the authors concluded that the AI-integrated, competency-oriented problem-based and case-based learning model was associated with higher short-term scores in theoretical knowledge, practical skills, critical-thinking disposition, clinical performance, and teaching satisfaction when compared to conventional instruction. Nevertheless, the study highlighted several key methodological boundaries that necessitate cautious interpretation. The trial was conducted as a single-center study, involved a relatively limited sample size of 106 trainees, and featured a short intervention duration. Additionally, because the intervention combined multiple elements—including artificial intelligence tools, competency structuring, problem-based learning, and case-based learning—its multicomponent nature makes it challenging to isolate the specific contribution of each component. Consequently, the researchers emphasized that further multicenter studies with longer follow-up periods are required to confirm whether these educational benefits can be sustained over time and generalized to broader clinical training environments.

Subject of Research: Artificial intelligence-integrated clinical teaching in ophthalmology education

Article Title: The application of a problem-based learning and case-based learning teaching model supported by artificial intelligence and structured around job competency in ophthalmology clinical teaching

Article References: Zhipeng, W., & Long, L. (2026). The application of a problem-based learning and case-based learning teaching model supported by artificial intelligence and structured around job competency in ophthalmology clinical teaching. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-10687-9

Keywords: ophthalmology education, problem-based learning, case-based learning, artificial intelligence in education, clinical teaching, job competency, Chinese Clinical Physician Post Competency Questionnaire, critical thinking, CTDI-CV, clinical practice ability, Mini-CEX, theoretical knowledge assessment, practical skills evaluation, teaching satisfaction, First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, medical trainee education, randomized controlled trial

cim: Mérhetően javítja az orvostanhallgatók teljesítményét az AI-alapú oktatás
lead: Egy 106 fős klinikai kísérlet szerint a mesterséges intelligenciával támogatott, esetalapú oktatás jelentősen növelte a szemész rezidensek vizsgaeredményeit.
osszefoglalo:
A Csengcsoui Egyetem Első Számú Egyetemi Kórházának kutatói 2 éves kísérletben vizsgálták a mesterséges intelligencia hatékonyságát az orvosképzésben. A 106 szemész rezidenst két csoportra osztották: a kontrollcsoport hagyományos előadásokat és feladatorientált képzést kapott, míg a másik csoport képzését **AI-eszközökkel és esetalapú tanulással** egészítették ki.

A tesztidőszak végén az AI-alapú tananyagot használó hallgatók **szignifikánsan jobb eredményt értek el** mind az elméleti tudásfelmérésben, mind a gyakorlati vizsgákon. A résztvevők emellett magasabb pontszámot kaptak a kritikai gondolkodást és a közvetlen klinikai teljesítményt mérő teszteken is.

A kutatók kiemelték, hogy az eredmények egyelőre rövid távúak és egyetlen intézményre korlátozódnak. A módszer hosszú távú hatásainak és széles körű alkalmazhatóságának igazolásához további, több központban végzett vizsgálatokra lesz szükség.
miert_szamit: Az eredmények megmutatják, hogy az AI nemcsak a napi munkafolyamatok gyorsítására, hanem **a szakképzés és a gyakorlati oktatás hatékonyságának növelésére** is közvetlenül használható.

prioritas.indok: Randomizált klinikai oktatási kísérlet konkrét és mérhető eredményekkel a szemészetben Forrás-tapasztalat: -6.
prioritas.cim_hu: Hatékonyabbá tette a szemészképzést az AI-alapú oktatási modell egy új kutatás szerint
prioritas.lead_hu: Egy randomizált vizsgálat kimutatta, hogy a mesterséges intelligenciával támogatott képzés jobb elméleti és gyakorlati eredményeket hozott a szemészeti oktatásban a hagyományos módszereknél.

tenyellenorzes.esemeny: A Csengcsoui Egyetem Első Számú Egyetemi Kórházának kutatói egy 106 fős klinikai kísérletben kimutatták, hogy a mesterséges intelligenciával támogatott, kompetenciaalapú és esetalapú oktatás rövid távon szignifikánsan javította a szemész rezidensek elméleti, gyakorlati és klinikai vizsgaeredményeit a hagyományos oktatáshoz képest.
